sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Torah being an inheritance for every Jew stems from the aspect of Yaakov within them, while the command to prepare oneself to learn Torah as a non-inheritance relates to the aspect of Yisrael, and the gift of Torah relates to the aspect of Yeshurun.

translations.translation: And this is: "Torah tzivah... morashah kehilas Yaakov. Vayehi biYeshurun melech... yachad shivtei Yisrael."
That the Torah is an inheritance for every Jew is from the aspect of Yaakov within them
("morashah kehilas Yaakov").
And the concept of "prepare yourself to learn Torah," which is not an inheritance for you, is from the aspect of Yisrael,
and the gift of Torah is from the aspect of Yeshurun.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between Yaakov, the aspect of a servant who works to rectify the concealment of the name Elokim, and Yisrael, the aspect of a son who rules over Elokim, corresponding to the weekdays and Shabbos respectively.

translations.translation: The explanation is:
Yaakov is the aspect of a servant, as it is written,34
"Hearken to Me, Yaakov My servant,"
and Yisrael is the aspect of a son, as it is written,35
"My firstborn son Yisrael."36
And the service of Yaakov is37
that he serves G-d,
to rectify the concealment that comes from the name Elokim.
And Yisrael is from the term "for you have striven with G-d,"38
meaning he rules and dominates over the name Elokim.
And this is what is stated in the Zohar,39
that Yisrael and Yaakov correspond to the two names Havayah and Elokim.
For regarding the aspect of Yaakov—"Yud, ekev" (heel)40—
there is the concealment of the name Elokim, and his service is to rectify the concealment.
And even after he rectifies the concealment of the name Elokim,
through which the revelation of Havayah is drawn down,
it is the revelation of Havayah as it is through the name Elokim.
But Yisrael, which is from the term "for you have striven with G-d,"
for whom there is no initial concealment or hiding of the name Elokim,
the revelation of Havayah drawn down through Yisrael is the revelation of Havayah itself.
And it is explained in Likkutei Torah41
that the service during the six weekdays is
(generally)
the service of Yaakov,
the service of refinement,
to rectify the concealment of the name Elokim.
And the service of Shabbos is in the aspect of Yisrael.
For on Shabbos it is written,42
"And Elokim completed,"
meaning the measure of contraction and concealment of the name Elokim ceased, and the revelation of Havayah is drawn down,
and therefore there is no need then for the service of refinement,
and the service of Shabbos is to delight in Havayah,
which is above the service of refinement.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Yeshurun is higher than Yisrael, representing the essence of the soul as it is rooted in the Atzmus of the Infinite One, like a song without beginning or end, which is revealed on Rosh Hashanah.

translations.translation: And the aspect of Yeshurun is higher even than the aspect of Yisrael.
For Yeshurun is from the term "shir" (song),
a round thing like a ring that has no beginning or end.43
And it is explained in Likkutei Torah44
that Yisrael is called by the name Yeshurun from the aspect of the root of souls as they arose in thought.
And it can be said
that the difference between Yeshurun and Yisrael,
even though the concept of Yisrael—"for you have striven with G-d"—is also from the revelation of the root of the soul that is above its enclothing in the body
[as explained in many places45
that Yaakov is the soul enclothed in the body, and Yisrael is the root of the soul above its enclothing in the body],
for Yisrael is the aspect of a son
(as above),
and the term and concept of "son" applies specifically after the son is drawn from the father's brain,
but Yeshurun is the essence of the soul as it is rooted in His very Essence,
analogous to the son as he is within the father's brain itself
(before being drawn forth).
And this is that Yeshurun is from the term "shir" (song) that has no beginning or end,
for in the level of souls as they have already been drawn from the father's brain
(even as they are above)
there are distinctions of levels,
but the concept of a song that has no beginning or end is in the essence of souls as they are rooted in the Ein Sof.
And this is the meaning of "Vayehi biYeshurun melech," and it is stated in Likkutei Torah44
that this refers to Rosh Hashanah,
"Make Me king over you,"
for the concept of "Make Me king over you" is through the revelation of the essence of the soul as it is rooted in the Atzmus of Ein Sof.
